reason: The law was adopted in February 2020 and took effect that month, but controllers and processors had an 18-month transition that ended in August 2021, when the Commission dates full application. Items saying it took effect in February 2020 therefore describe entry into force, not full application.

The Commission found the Agency executing its new powers once the transition ended, and the Agency's 2025 report gives specifics: 196 supervisions and 121 decisions ordering violations to be removed. Application is real but weak: supervisions found low compliance, other laws are not fully aligned, the Commission records no progress in 2025, a lack of budgetary independence and a NATO transfer amendment, none of which is repeal or suspension. Article 122 in the unofficial translation (provisions 'cease to apply until' accession) contradicts all this evidence, looks like a translation fault and should be checked against the Macedonian text.
The Commission's 2024 report says the law still needs to be adopted, and the Reform Agenda sets a June 2025 target, so the law was planned at this date.

The law was adopted on 27 June 2025, published on 4 July 2025, entered into force on the eighth day and applies from 1 January 2026, except that entities in Art. 4(2) points 8 to 16 are covered only from EU accession. No item shows the measures it requires, such as the by-laws (due within six months), the entity lists, or the government team and network (due within twelve months, so by July 2026), and MKD-CIRT predates the law; the regulator's 'applies' statement gives the legal status only. 'Proposal' in GOV-2026-002-0097 comes from an annex of 2025 opinions, so it is historic rather than a conflict, and the Commission's finding that alignment is incomplete concerns content, not status.

This holds for the 2019 framework only, which has applied since 1 September 2020 (electronic documents from 20 December 2019): the Commission's May 2026 assessment records by-laws from 2020, two trust service providers accredited in 2021 and registered, and ministry supervisory inspections. The June 2025 eIDAS 2 amendment, including the digital wallet, is in force but applies only from 1 June 2027, so that part is adopted and not applied at the freeze date, and no item shows its by-laws were adopted. Use is narrow: the Commission found the trusted list step not achieved and the Government still calls for full application of the law.
The Commission's 2024 report says North Macedonia has yet to adopt the national cybersecurity strategy, and the Reform Agenda plans an updated strategy by June 2025.

The Government adopted the strategy on 21 January 2025, which the Commission confirms; a February 2025 Commission item still planning adoption is out of date. The only item saying more is the Agency for Electronic Communications' one-line status that the strategy 'is applied', which is government reporting without specifics, comes from a body other than the lead ministry, and which I have not accepted, so the reviewer should decide. The new cyber security law is one delivered measure, but no item reports wider delivery or the half-yearly reports the strategy promises.
The Reform Agenda plans adoption of a new law by June 2025, so the law was planned at this date.

The law was adopted on 27 June 2025 and amended on 29 December 2025; it entered into force on the eighth day after publication on 4 July 2025 and was due to apply from 1 June 2026, but no later item confirms application or reports measures under it, and the security supervision reported for 2025 rests on the earlier law. By-laws were due within 15 months (October 2026) and operators have 18 months to align (January 2027), so that deadline has not yet passed. The Commission's May 2026 finding that the step is not achieved, with a grace period to 30 June 2026 whose outcome is not in the evidence, concerns alignment, and 'draft' or 'proposal' wording in GOV-2025-004-0172 and GOV-2026-002-0100 is historic rather than a conflict.

The plan's own rows are planned activities, but the Commission states that the Government adopted the accompanying action plan on 21 January 2025, so the plan as a whole is adopted (the Commission labels it 2025-2028, the document 2025-2027). Only one row is shown delivered, the cyber security law, adopted in June 2025. No item reports on other rows, including those due by end 2025, so nothing supports implemented.
